Header: Eichhornia crassipes English: lilac devil, Nile lily, pickerelweed, water hyacinth, water orchid

Prevention: Minimise the level of nutrients in water by planting trees to stablise ground near rice fields and limiting fertilizer use
Monitoring: Free-floating, aquatic plant that may be anchored in shallow water.
Leaves: dark green, shiny, hairless, oval to egg-shaped to almost rounded (2-25 cm long and 2-15 cm wide), thick and shiny; swollen bladder-like stems (30 cm long)
Flowers: pale violet or blue (4-6 cm long and 3.5-5 cm wide); clusters of 8-10
Fruit: capsules (a dry fruit that opens at maturity) (10-15 mm long), containing very fine seeds
Runners: 10 cm long, produced across the water surface to give rise to new plants
Look for this weed in irrigation channels, dams, ponds, floodplains, swamps, wetlands and slow-moving rivers
Direct Control: Small infestations can be manually removed, including adults and eggs
Do not mechanically chop or shred the weed - this creates fragments which can form new plants
Biological control agents include: the mite
